The best first step is a **controlled final-position rank probe** that tests whether SASRec distinguishes direct continuations from plausible adjacent items. No diagnostic results or validation improvements are available yet.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Training margins depend on score scale and sampled negatives. Fixed-candidate ranks make comparisons across model variants easier to interpret. (2) Current probes aggregate sequence positions. Inspecting the final valid position better matches next-item recommendation. (3) Feedback identifies weak adjacent-interest recommendations and insufficient recent-interest specificity. These observations motivate targeted challenges, but do not establish compatibility, ownership satisfaction, or causal preferences.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Sampling research [1,2] shows that negative selection can affect model comparisons. Diagnostic candidate distributions must therefore remain fixed and separate from benchmark evaluation. (2) History-edit research [3] motivates recommendation sensitivity tests. Controlled deletions measure model dependence, without identifying causal user intent. (3) The TREC recommendation rubric [4] separates compatibility uncertainty from incompatibility. Missing title or description evidence should remain unknown.

These insights define three research directions: ranking discrimination, history dependence, and evidence sufficiency.

| Direction | Existing approach | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discrimination | Training score margins | Frozen final-position rank challenges | Relationship to validation gains |
| Dependence | History edits [3] | Equal-count random deletion controls | Causal interpretation |
| Evidence | Compatibility rubric [4] | Source-linked labels with abstention | Sparse public attributes |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/future potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

1. **Controlled rank probe — 5/8/3.** Originality: useful task-specific combination; established components. Potential: reusable across architectures; predictive value remains untested. Difficulty: uses existing hooks; candidate freezing requires care. Inspired by [1,2].
2. **Controlled history deletion — 6/8/5.** Originality: combines content groups with random controls; history interventions already exist. Potential: identifies interference hypotheses; positional effects complicate conclusions. Difficulty: inference-only implementation; masking and compaction need separate handling. Inspired by [3].
3. **Evidence-linked recommendation audit — 5/7/6.** Originality: connects feedback to source evidence; annotation frameworks already exist. Potential: exposes unsupported compatibility assumptions; metadata may be insufficient. Difficulty: simple schema; reliable evidence extraction is demanding. Inspired by [4].

At 0% progress, select **idea 1** for its feasibility and architecture compatibility.

```text
freeze deterministic training prefix/next-item records
for each target, freeze equal-sized distractor sets:
    training-sampler, popularity-matched, text-similar
for each trained model and frozen record:
    features = log2feats(prefix)[last_valid_position]
    scores = predict_score(features, candidates)
    record target rank using deterministic tie-breaking
aggregate ranks and coverage separately by dataset and challenge
return metrics and explicit metric_definitions
```

Use training-only popularity and TF-IDF over permitted titles/descriptions; fetch no weights. Exclude observed user interactions from distractors and report insufficient pools explicitly. Unobserved distractors have unknown relevance. Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)`, `run_full_diagnosis(train_loader)`, and `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis)`; evaluate `view.model` without gradients and restore its mode. Report missing measurements as unavailable. Retain all four dataset routes, seeds, artifact constraints, and pinned macro validation HR@10 for selection; diagnostic ranks never replace it.

idea.description: Add deterministic final-position ranking challenges to the compatibility-preserving diagnostic adapter. Evaluate the same training-derived prefix/target records against separately frozen training-sampler, popularity-matched, and title/description-similar distractor sets.
idea.motivation: The existing margin probes mix sequence positions and depend on score scale and negative sampling. Controlled ranks can reveal whether apparent separation persists against plausible adjacent items, addressing the reported failure mode without assuming unavailable compatibility information or user traits.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Construct diagnostic records exclusively from training interactions, ensuring targets are absent from their input prefixes. Use the final valid sequence representation through the compatibility hooks, adapting feature extraction when architecture changes. Freeze records, candidate IDs, tie-breaking, and seeds across trials; persist artifacts beneath the trial directory. Compute popularity from training histories and optional TF-IDF similarity from available titles/descriptions only. Match candidate counts across challenge types; explicitly report insufficient pools, missing metadata, record counts, and coverage. Treat distractors as items with unknown relevance. Use view.model.eval() under torch.no_grad(), restoring its prior mode afterward. Return measured metrics and definitions with unavailable values represented explicitly. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, and the host evaluator. Any subsequent architecture change must update the predictor writer. Select models solely using pinned macro validation HR@10; make no claims about unseen test performance or simulator traits.
idea.pseudocode:
records = freeze_training_prefix_target_records(seed=42)
challenges = freeze_candidate_sets(records, training_popularity, optional_training_text_index, seed=42)
previous_mode = view.model.training
view.model.eval()
try:
    with torch.no_grad():
        for record in records:
            features = view.log2feats(record.prefix)
            final_feature = select_last_valid_position(features, record.prefix)
            for challenge in challenges[record.id]:
                scores = view.predict_score(final_feature, challenge.item_ids)
                rank = deterministic_target_rank(scores, challenge.target_index)
                accumulate(record.dataset, challenge.type, rank)
finally:
    view.model.train(previous_mode)
return {'metrics': aggregate_with_coverage(), 'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions()}

originality.positive: Combines architecture-compatible final-position probes with controlled distractor distributions tailored to the observed adjacent-interest failure.
originality.negative: Ranking diagnostics, popularity matching, and text-based distractor construction are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Provides a reusable basis for controlled architecture and loss ablations across all four datasets.
future_potential.negative: Whether diagnostic improvements predict validation HR@10 improvements remains an empirical question.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing feature and scoring hooks without requiring model retraining or external weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct target alignment, deterministic candidate persistence, and architecture-specific feature extraction require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] Sampling reliability research referenced in the supplied search results
contributions: Reports that sampling bias can change relative model rankings, motivating fixed diagnostic candidate sets.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed diagnostic predicts validation improvements.
Sampled rankings do not establish full-catalog recommendation quality.

related_work.title: [2] Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study referenced in the supplied search results
contributions: Examines interactions between negative-sampling methods and dataset popularity bias using repeated experiments and hyperparameter optimization.
limitations: Its reported experimental setting does not validate the proposed four-category diagnostic protocol.

related_work.title: [3] Scarcelli et al. (2025), interaction-history editing research
contributions: Searches for minimal interaction-history edits that change recommendations, motivating controlled sensitivity probes.
limitations: Recommendation changes after history edits do not identify causal user preferences.

related_work.title: [4] TREC Product Recommendation 2025 annotation rubric
contributions: Distinguishes substitutes, related products, and complements, including compatible, unknown-compatibility, and incompatible cases.
limitations: The rubric does not supply missing product attributes or validate automated annotations for the twenty training users.
